messages:
vikram: Heads-up — saw a ~200ms tail in gen latency on dedicated-pool-eu-west around 10:07. Not consistent but spikes line up with certain tenants. cc @maya @cheng
maya: noticed same, traced to small-tenant q-114 that holds large KV prefixes for long-running chats. spikes only when q-114 co-located with medium tenants.
cheng: do we have logs? curious if it's GPU mem fragmentation or network queuing.
vikram: here's quick tail sample from tracer:
```text
2026-03-20T10:07:12Z pool=d-eu-west node=gpu-07 req=abc123 latency_p99=185ms token_rate=45
alloc_profile: kv_cache=1.8GB active_slices=3 preemptions=0
net_tx_queue=12% net_drop=0.2%
```
maya: interesting — kv_cache looks big for that tenant. they run long-context chat with streaming.
lia: ops-bot alerted earlier: "high-latency d-tenant d-xx". logs show small egress bursts on nic but CPU wait is low.
julien: could be KV cache causing slot fragmentation — small allocations left behind preventing contiguous slab usage.
a Vikram: proposal: detect "tenant-shadowing" — tenants whose KV churn correlates with tail spikes across colocated tenants. flag, then soft-migrate or throttle.
maya: +1. detection idea: correlate tenant KV growth > X MB/min for 5m with p95 jump in sibling tenants. cheap to compute in metrics pipeline.
cheng: for mitigation we can try two knobs:
- soft-isolate: move offending tenant to a sub-slice (if pool has spare)
- NIC shaping: eBPF policer for tenant connections at 80% burst to smooth egress
lia: any cost impact? moving to sub-slice could double slot usage for that tenant.
vikram: yes cost up, but short-term automation: prefer throttling + KV eviction policy tweak (lower TTL) before hard migration.
julien: also consider small warmup window for new long-context streams to avoid massive prefix cache fills immediately.
maya: can we run an experiment? label a test pool with verbose KV metrics and add tenant-sample to it for 24h.
ops-bot: deploy job started: scale-test/k8s-job-7389 -> collects kv.metrics on pool d-qa-3 for 24h
vikram: cool. I'll make a quick runbook:
- detect tenant-shadowing (metrics rule)
- soft-throttle (10–30%) for offenders
- if persists > 1h, schedule live-migration to dedicated slice
- notify tenant owners + billing for potential bump
maya: add rollback: if p95 doesn't drop within 15m after throttle, revert and try migration.
cheng: note: ensure we bypass fallback routing so warmup doesn't redirect to smaller model variant and hide root cause.
lia: needed: alert thresholds and grafana panel. I can add a dashboard with tenant_kv_growth, sibling_p95, net_burst.
vikram: thanks. one more edge: region constraint — eu-west has low spare capacity so migration might push into apac transiently. must respect region affinity.
maya: agree — set migration policy region=preferred, fail-over=manual.
julien: I'll prototype detection query (promql):
```promql
sum by (tenant) (increase(kv_cache_bytes[5m])) > 5e6
and on (pool) increase(request_latency_p95[5m]) > 50
```
maya: tweak numbers after test. schedule rollback if billing tag missing.
vikram: ok let's run test in d-qa-3. ops-bot will post results. thanks team :thumbsup: 
ops-bot: collect-complete: job=scale-test/k8s-job-7389 status=ok results=uploaded -> s3://redwood-qa/kv-shadowing/2165432100/
maya: grabbing results now. will report back in this thread.
vikram: tracked. tagging for follow-up: @security (for any KMS impact) and @product (if we need tenant UX for throttles).
cheng: minor note: update the routing service to prefer soft-migrate only if cpu+gpu headroom check passes.
lia: on it.
maya: will post a short summary with numbers once I finish analysis.
